title: Check: etcd backup and restore
description: Five questions on the exam's most reliable task.

questions.prompt: Write the etcdctl subcommand and flag that takes a snapshot to /tmp/etcd.db (omit the cert flags).
questions.explanation: The full form also needs --endpoints, --cacert, --cert and --key, all readable from /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml.

questions.prompt: Which API version must etcdctl use for snapshots?

options.text: It is chosen automatically in every version

questions.explanation: Version 3 is required. Recent etcdctl defaults to it, but setting it explicitly costs nothing and removes a whole class of exam failure.

questions.prompt: Where do you find the certificate paths for the etcdctl flags?
questions.explanation: The static Pod manifest lists exactly the --cacert, --cert and --key the server itself uses.

questions.prompt: After `etcdctl snapshot restore` into a new data directory, what must you do?

options.text: Point the etcd static Pod's data directory at the restored one and let the kubelet restart it

questions.explanation: Restore only writes files. Editing the manifest is what makes etcd use them.

questions.prompt: What does an etcd snapshot contain?

options.text: The entire cluster state - every object

questions.explanation: Which is why it is the one backup that matters, and why the file deserves the same protection as the cluster.
